messages.subject: sidebars & sliders - questiions
parts:
Two simple (I think) questions -

1) the Shiny app I'm building largely works on data in an input csv file, has a sidebar for loading in said datafile, and then various tabs for various things.
I want the file loading sidebar visible when any of the tab panels is chosen (which it is).  But, can one of my tab panels also have its very own sidebar?

2) In this same app, I would like, in just one of the tabbed panels, to have a silder control, however, I want the slider min and max to be variable, based
on the current csv-read data.  I'm not sure how to (or if I even can) do that, based on the tutorials.  Meaning, how do I effectively 'pass' the determined values
to use from server.R to ui.R?

thanks!

messages.author: 4be88a5fc86a040f
messages.subject: Re: sidebars & sliders - questiions
parts:
I believe both questions were asked in this group.
1) Can be done with conditional panels. The sidebar panel stays the same, but elements turn visible when a specific tab panel active. Items that are not placed inside conditional panel would be shared across all tabs. For this you need to specify JavaScript condition like "input.tabset_id == 'tabPanel_value' ". e.g. UI.R:
 sidebarPanel
        (
            textInput("sharedText", "Shared textbox","")
            # insert other controls shared across tabs

            conditionalPanel # Elements displayed when tab with value "First" active
            (
                condition = "input.tabMain == 'First'"
                #... insert controls you need to show when First tab active
            ),
            conditionalPanel # Elements displayed when tab with value "Second" active
            (
                condition = "input.tabMain == 'Second'"
                #... insert controls you need to show when Second tab active
            )     
        ),
        mainPanel
        (
            tabsetPanel
            (
                id = "tabMain",
                tabPanel
                (
                     title = "first",
                     value = "First"
                     #....
                ),              
                tabPanel
                (
                     title = "second",
                     value = "Second"
                )              
            )

2) You can use renderUI for this. Define slider in ui.r as uiOutput and write the logic in renderUI. Assuming user selected data is a reactive that returns NULL when nothing selected:
ui.r
  sidebarPanel(
    uiOutput("mySlider")
  )

in server.R
  output$mySlider <- renderUI({
    if (!is.null(myData()))
      sliderInput("mySlider", "test", min = 0, max = nrow(myData()), value = 0)
    else NULL
      })

server.r, assuming your data is stored in dataframe named "df"
